source.title: Grokking or Glitching? How Low-Precision Drives Slingshot Loss Spikes
source.authors: Hanqing Liu; Jian Cao; Yuan-Ze Li; Zi-Jian Zhou

record.file_problem: The full paper text, including appendices, is present. The text gives arXiv metadata for 2026 and states that the paper is for NeurIPS 2026.
record.tranche_reason: The paper tests numerical-precision and optimizer interventions on Slingshot spikes, and argues that Slingshots are a finite-precision artifact rather than an intrinsic optimizer dynamic. It also reports a modular-division result relating spikes to test-accuracy gains.
record.gate_note: The paper reports a modular-division test-accuracy trajectory and multiple Slingshot interventions. The claimed CIFAR-10 dataset-size results concern whether spikes occur, not grokking delay; LLM logit divergence is not a measure of delayed generalization. Rows for the latter are recorded only as findings fitting no version.
record.test_reason: Only Figure 2c bears on a version. Unregularized Adam training on modular division (p=97, 50/50 split) shows test accuracy rising stepwise with each Slingshot spike to 100%. That bears on V1 in a no-weight-decay setting. Every other experiment measures whether Slingshot loss spikes occur, not whether delayed generalization occurs or disappears. So the precision and optimizer interventions do not test V7 as stated, which concerns the generalization delay.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors also interpret Slingshot spikes as implicit perturbations that may help modular-division models reach generalizing solutions. They state that SC and NFI appear in large-model training.
record.recipe_differences: Uses the Slingshot study framework and modular-division setting, while adding precision, zero-sum projection, optimizer, normalization, CIFAR-10, and language-modeling experiments; it is not a direct replication of the original grokking studies.
record.method_sensitivity: Spike occurrence changes with numerical precision, Adam epsilon, optimizer step size, normalization placement, architecture, batch regime, and learning rate. Float64 loss computation removes spikes in the reported classification setting; ResNet18 and mini-batch VGG11 do not show visible spikes.

fits_no_version.finding: Slingshot loss spikes in unregularized CE+Adam training disappear with float64, or with float64 logits/loss only. They also disappear under zero-sum gradient projection, Adam epsilon 1e-5 and BN before the classifier. They persist under a logit clamp that rules out underflow, are absent in ResNet18 and in mini-batch VGG11, and occur at all tested CIFAR-10 subset sizes.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Slingshot loss spikes are a finite-precision artifact: Softmax Collapse breaks the zero-sum gradient constraint, causing Numerical Feature Inflation.

fits_no_version.finding: In FineWeb nanoGPT training, mean logit after 1e5 steps is 183 with float32 loss and 498 with float64 loss. The authors attribute this to token-frequency imbalance in output embeddings.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Late-stage LLM logit growth is driven by the output-embedding global mean and is not reduced by higher-precision loss computation.

record.problems: The paper does not report uncertainty estimates for the results relevant here. The Figure 2c result is described qualitatively without exact test-accuracy values or timing relative to training-accuracy saturation. The numerical-intervention figure does not identify the model or dataset in its caption/text. The CIFAR-10 test set is stated to contain 1,000 samples.
record.rows_left_out: No additional relevant reported result rows were left out.

untested.parts: Start at chance, the delay after training accuracy saturates, and the dependence of the delay on training-set size.

Whether the generalization delay (test-accuracy jump) disappears under float64, zero-sum projection, larger Adam epsilon or pre-classifier BN. Only loss-spike occurrence is measured under these controls.
Not tested. CIFAR-10 runs measure spikes, not delayed generalization.
Not tested. The LLM runs measure logit growth and the Softmax Collapse fraction.

record.verdict_notes: The record's V7 'supports' labels conflate spike removal with removal of the grokking delay. The paper never reports test accuracy or generalization timing under the precision or optimizer controls, so no V7 verdict is given. Its own account, that spikes drive stepwise test-accuracy gains, would if anything predict that controlling precision changes unregularized CE grokking. That was not measured. No uncertainty estimates; single seed (42).

versions.untested_parts: Reports that modular-division test accuracy rises stepwise with Slingshot spikes and eventually reaches 100%; it does not state that test accuracy starts at chance, quantify how long after training accuracy saturates the rise begins, or test whether the delay grows as an algorithmic training set shrinks.

The paper proposes Numerical Feature Inflation, but does not test whether a generalizing circuit forms gradually, memorizing components are removed later, or circuit progress measures anticipate a generalization jump.

The paper tests Slingshot and numerical effects on CIFAR-10 and language modeling, not delayed generalization on non-algorithmic data or switching grokking-like delays through initialization scale or weight norm.
The paper trains a nanoGPT-style model on FineWeb and measures Softmax Collapse and logit growth, not delayed generalization during realistic LLM pretraining or fine-tuning.
The paper does not test whether low-norm bias selects a more efficient circuit, or whether a critical dataset size or ungrokking follows.
The paper does not compare whether runs converge to the same identifiable algorithm.
Tests precision, gradient projection, optimizer, and other interventions on Slingshot spikes. It does not establish that every delayed-generalization phenomenon is caused by these effects.

rows.note: The paper describes the pattern in text but does not give exact accuracy values at each spike or the timing relative to training-accuracy saturation.
rows.check: The conditions are recoverable from Appendix D.1: 2-layer Transformer or 6-layer MLP, Adam lr 1e-3, no weight decay, float32, 100k steps, 50% train split. source_check.correct: Figure 2c reports modular-division test accuracy increasing in steps associated with loss spikes, eventually reaching 100%. Its architecture is not explicitly identified; the modular experiments use a 2-layer decoder-only Transformer and a 6-layer MLP. Appendix D.1 specifies p=97, a 50/50 training/validation split, Adam, cross-entropy, learning rate 0.001, zero weight decay, batch size 512, 100,000 steps and float32.

rows.subject: VGG11 on CIFAR-10
rows.stage_stated: trained from scratch; other stage details not stated
rows.operation_detail: Applied Batch Normalization immediately before the final classifier.
rows.baseline: VGG11 with Batch Normalization inside convolutional layers still exhibits spikes.
rows.value: Applying Batch Normalization before the classifier eliminates the instability and stabilizes training at the zero-loss Softmax Collapse state.
rows.note: The paper attributes the effect to centering batch features and removing the global-mean drift component.
rows.check: Spike elimination only.

rows.subject: not stated (label-smoothing experiment)

rows.operation_detail: Applied label smoothing.
rows.measure: Precision-induced NFI Slingshot spikes and other loss spikes.
rows.value: Label smoothing eliminates precision-induced NFI spikes but introduces a separate class of loss spikes attributed to Edge of Stability.
rows.locator: Figure 4b, Section 4.2, Label Smoothing, and Appendix C.4.3

rows.subject: VGG11 on CIFAR-10
rows.stage_stated: training for 10^6 steps
rows.operation_detail: Trained with mini-batches of size 256.
rows.measure: Softmax Collapse frequency, visible Slingshot spikes, and late-stage NFI growth.
rows.baseline: Full-batch setting discussed as the comparison.
rows.value: Approximately half of samples enter Softmax Collapse with exactly zero loss; no Slingshot spike is observed, but NFI still causes rapid late-stage growth of the global feature mean and logits.
rows.note: The paper says non-collapsed samples maintain gradients and Adam moment estimates, preventing a sudden effective-learning-rate increase.
rows.check: Softmax Collapse fraction and NFI growth under mini-batch training; not grokking.

rows.subject: not stated (model in underflow-clamping experiment)
rows.stage_stated: training; other details not stated
rows.operation_detail: Clamped logits so the minimum logit remained no more than 100 below the maximum.
rows.measure: Presence of Slingshot spikes while gradients remain in float32's representable range.
rows.value: Slingshot spikes persist despite the clamp.
rows.note: The paper uses this result to distinguish mantissa absorption from exponent-based underflow.
rows.check: Spike persistence under a logit clamp; not grokking delay.
